# Sirach Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 22 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**22:1** The sluggard is like a stone smeared with dung — everyone wrinkles their nose at the disgrace.

**22:2** The sluggard is like a pile of manure on the heap — whoever picks it up wipes their hands clean fast.

**22:3** A father is disgraced when he raises an undisciplined son; a foolish daughter is born to his ruin.

**22:4** A sensible daughter will find a husband; one who shames the family is a wound in her father's heart.

**22:5** A shameless woman humiliates both father and husband; both will despise her.

**22:6** Speaking at the wrong moment is like playing music at a funeral; but correction and instruction are always welcome.

**22:7** Teaching a fool is like trying to glue a shattered pot back together, or trying to wake someone from a coma.

**22:8** Tell something important to a fool and you're speaking to a man half-asleep; at the end he'll just say, "Wait, what?"

**22:9** Grieve for the dead — the light has gone out. Grieve for the fool — his mind has gone out. But grieve more gently for the dead, because at least the dead are at rest. A fool's life is worse than death.

**22:10** You mourn for the dead seven days; but you mourn for a fool and a godless person all the days of their lives.

**22:11** Don't waste words on a fool; don't go looking for company among the senseless. Keep your distance from them — it will save you trouble and keep you clean. Stay away and you'll find peace; you won't wear yourself out in their nonsense.

**22:12** What's heavier than lead? A fool — that's the name for it.

**22:13** Sand and salt and a block of iron are easier to carry than a person without sense.

**22:14** Just as beams lashed together inside a building won't come loose even in an earthquake, a heart grounded in careful counsel won't be shaken.

**22:15** A thought founded on deep understanding is like fine smooth plaster on a wall.

**22:16** Small stones balanced high up won't hold against the wind; a cowardly heart entertained by a fool won't hold against fear.

**22:17** A heart that has been wounded by insight is like a wall that has been struck. It cannot stand when any fear comes against it.

**22:18** A heart anchored in careful reflection is like plaster on a smooth wall — it holds.

**22:19** Throwing pebbles at birds scatters them; heaping reproach on a friend scatters the friendship.

**22:20** If you drew a sword on a friend, don't give up — there is a way back. If you said something harsh to a friend, don't panic — you can still make peace. But insults, arrogance, betraying a secret, a treacherous attack — those things make a friend run and not return.

**22:21** Stick with your neighbor when he's poor, and you'll get to celebrate when he prospers. Stand by him when things are hard, and you'll have a share in what he inherits.

**22:22** Smoke and steam come before the fire of a furnace; quarreling comes before bloodshed.

**22:23** I won't be ashamed to shelter a friend, or to show my face when things are bad.

**22:24** And if I suffer for it, everyone who hears will know to be on guard against that person.

**22:25** Who will put a sentinel at my mouth and a seal on my lips, so that my words don't bring me down and my tongue doesn't wreck everything?

**22:26** LORD, Father and Master of my life — don't abandon me to my own worst counsel, and don't let me fall because of my words.

**22:27** Who will assign a whip to my thoughts and wisdom's discipline over my heart — to spare me nothing in my foolishness, not letting any sin slip by unchallenged?
